Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.
2.
Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner No.1 t o 3 are the sons, petitioner No.4 and 5 are the daughter of late Shafiulla baig.

That on 10.03.202 at about 07.30 PM., Shafiulla Baig was crossing the road near Kolar _ Bangalore NH-75 road, near MVJ Hospital, Hosakote, wherein the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-03-ND-4682 drove it, with high speed rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Shifiulla and caused the accident, in the accident,
Shafiulla Baig sustained grievous injuries, he was shifted to Srinivasas Hospital,
wherein the doctor declared him as brought dead.
Autopsy was conducted at Govt Hospital, Hosakote.
Petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that Late.Shafiulla Baig was aged about 71 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was scarp merchant and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.79/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the of the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents appeared through their counsel, filed vakalath and written statement.

On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 10.03.2024 at about 07.30 PM., the deceased shafiullah Baig was crossing the Kolar- Bangalore NH-75 road, near MVJ Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore, wherein the driver of the Car bearing Reg No.KA-03-ND-4682 drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, due to which, he sustained grievous injuries and died on the way to the hospital as alleged in the plaint?

2.Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?

Addl Issue No.1:
Whether the respondent No.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions and accident due to the negligent act of the deceased as contended in the written statement?

 REASONS 10. Issues No.1, Addl Issue No.1 & Issue No.2:-
I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and son of the late Shafiulla Baig, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
11. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle that is respondent No.1.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, spot/ seizure mahazar, Inquest, IMV report, PM report and final report which are at Ex.P1 to 7 & 11.
12.
On perusal and analysis of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that Shafiulla Baig died due to the accidental injuries.
Ex.P.11 is the final report filed after fair investigation and it is not disputed by the respondent.
It is true that Usman.
S kalimulla
S / o Syed Kaleemulla respondent No.1 was the driver of the offending vehicle
. Seizure Mahazar, IMV report, final which are at Ex.P.3, 6, 11 reveals the involvement of the offending vehicle, and negligent act of its driver.
In the cross examination PW.1 nothing is suggested nor elicited any material facts to show that insured has violated the policy conditions and deceased died due to his negligent act.

13. Admittedly the accident occurred on 10.03.2024, petitioners have not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,500/-
has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2024.
14. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1953.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 71 years and future prospectus cannot be awarded.
Accordingly the multiplier 5 is applicable.
15. Deceased has left behind 5 dependents accordingly 1/4 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

1 Monthly income Rs.16,500/-

Rs.12,375 (income)X 12 (month) X 5 Rs.7,42,500/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.7,42,500/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
17. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

18 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

19. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

In the present case petitioner no.1 to 5 are the children of the deceased and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/-
each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation under this head.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

22. Liability:
The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, and they have failed to establish their contention as contended in the written statement.

Accordingly Respondent No.2 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
In the authorities relied on by the petitioner wherein it is categorically held that the legal heirs of the deceased are entitled for the compensation.
The aforesaid fact and the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased did not disputed by the respondents.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Addl Issue No.1 in the negative and issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
23. Issue No.3;
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.9,72,500/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 to 5 are entitled for Rs.1,94,500/- each with interest

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1 to 5 are permitted to withdraw their entire share of compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
